fragen.frage: Why does White move the king even though rooks are still on the board?
antworten: White is preparing to castle queenside.
Without queens the king is safe enough and becomes a strong piece in the center.
The king is meant to defend the rook on d1.
fragen.erklaerung: The endgame begins with the queen trade. Now every move counts by which the king reaches the center sooner.

fragen.frage: Why does White trade the queens?
antworten: After the trade White immediately wins the knight on b6.
With queens on the board an extra pawn is worth more than without.
The stronger side trades pieces: in the endgame the extra pawn weighs more.
fragen.erklaerung: The fewer pieces there are, the more clearly an extra pawn counts. On the queenside White can later create a passed pawn.

fragen.frage: Why is Qg7 mate and not just check?
antworten: The king on h8 may never capture a queen.
The king on h8 is in the corner, and there every check is mate.
The king on f6 defends the queen, and the king on h8 has no free square left.
fragen.erklaerung: A mate on the edge needs both pieces: the queen gives check, the king protects it from being captured.

fragen.frage: Why is the position a draw even though White is a pawn up?
antworten: The pawn on e3 is a rook's pawn.
White is stalemated.
Black has the opposition: White, to move, has to give way and reaches no key square.
fragen.erklaerung: The white king wants to go to d5, e5 or f5. As long as Black keeps the opposition, this route stays blocked for it.

fragen.erklaerung: First the king, then the pawn. Even 3. e4 would throw away the win here.

antworten: It takes the opposition.
It attacks the king on d6.
The king stands on a key square of the pawn on d2, no matter who moves next.
fragen.erklaerung: A key square is worth more than the opposition: once the king stands there, it wins as long as the pawn is not lost.

antworten: The pawn gives check and so gains a tempo.

fragen.erklaerung: Because the pawn reaches the 7th rank with check, the king has to go into the corner in front of the pawn. In the end Black has no move left.
